topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course structure, and the core learning objectives concerning environmental carcinogens and cancer mechanisms.

topics.label: Genetic, Endogenous, and Environmental Contributions to Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and evaluate how intrinsic endogenous mutations, inherited genetics, and environmental exposures interact to determine cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogens induce cancer, using the specific etiology and chromosomal translocation of Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how radiation, dietary toxins, and environmental hydrocarbons undergo metabolic processing to form DNA-damaging adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic pathways to cancer, exploring chronic inflammation, the distinction between cancer initiators and promoters, and the influence of host developmental timing.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic mutational signatures, population epidemiology, animal models, and in vitro assays used to evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Carcinogen Risk-Benefit Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture by summarizing environmental risk factors and considering the daily balance between carcinogenic risks and practical benefits.
